Posted June 26, 2001
(MarijuanaNews note: Last year, the South Australian state legislature went back and forth on reducing the number of plants that can be grown and still be subject only to a fine. First, the plant limit was cut from ten to three, then it was raised back to ten.
See
Common Sense Triumphs Over Prohibitionist Propaganda In South Australia – Plant Limit Raised Back To Ten from Three.

Then it was reduced back to three.

Now the prohibitionists, members of the Liberal?? Party, want to cut the limit to zero.

Other news from Australia shows that this is not only futile, it is also counterproductive. None of this seems to register with the prohibitionists.

In 1987 South Australia became the first state to move to a " cannabis expiation notice system. " However, while fining a person is better than jailing, the poor often cannot pay the fines and end up in jail.)

June 16, 2001
By Greg Kelton, State Political Reporter
LIBS WANT CANNABIS PLANT LIMIT DROPPED TO ZERO
Liberal backbenchers say they are close to forcing the State Government to toughen up the state's marijuana laws.
(MarijuanaNews note: In a Parliamentary system, " backbenchers " are members of the parliament who are not part of the government cabinet, nor of the opposition’s shadow cabinet.)

Senior Liberals, including ministers, are disturbed by the growing use of marijuana and want the three-plant limit dropped to zero.

Details of the mounting pressure in government ranks emerged as the Australian Democrats yesterday called for regulation, rather than continued prohibition, to help contain marijuana use.

While marijuana is still illegal in SA, people who grow three plants or less at home for personal use can escape a criminal sentence by paying an expiation fee.

Backbencher Martin Hamilton-Smith said marijuana use and growing of the drug in SA was " just a joke ".

Australian Democrats Leader Mike Elliott said governments should learn from the regulated use of alcohol and tobacco. He said research showed harsher penalties and more policing did not reduce marijuana use.

" The Democrats support the regulation approach because it will free up police resources, reduce drug-related crime, save government money and, most of all, because, as studies show, it will mean less people using marijuana, " he said.
(MarijuanaNews note: In fact, The Netherlands have a lower rate of marijuana use than does Australia, and there seems to be no consistent correlation between the severity of penalties and levels of use in either DEAland or Europe.

However, the level of marijuana use should never be the sole measure of success of the reform of the laws. The Dutch also have a much lower use of hard drugs than does Australia, the result of the separation of the markets. Would it be a bad thing if marijuana use went up and hard drug use went down?

Greece has the EU’s harshest marijuana laws, and a relatively low rate of marijuana use, but it also has a relatively high rate of solvent/inhalant use by younger teens, as does Australia. See the next item.)

Police Minister Robert Brokenshire said Mr Elliott should " come out into the electorate and talk to people whose children have been affected by marijuana use ".

" Most of the studies I have seen show that marijuana is the thin end of the wedge when it comes to drug use, " the minister said.
(MarijuanaNews note: How sad that someone so ignorant could be the " Police Minister. " )

" Potent " Cannabis Is A " commodity to swap for stronger drugs. "

and
 " Those who insist on keeping the plant illegal bear a serious degree of moral responsibility for young marijuana users who do go on to use cocaine, heroin, PCP or other genuinely dangerous or addictive drugs. "
Alan Bock, of the Orange County Register On the Real Gateway

From The Australian Broadcasting Company
http://www.abc.net.au
June 20, 2001

'Just Say No' drug campaign not getting through

The National Drug and Alcohol Research Centre says the " Just Say No to Drugs " campaign is failing more than ever.

Federal Government figures show that a third of 12-year-old school students have used inhalants such as glues and aerosol sprays.

Marijuana use is prevalent at schools with 11 per cent of 12-year-olds using cannabis, a figure rising to half the population at the age of 17.
(MarijuanaNews note: In other words, three times as many young Australians are using potentially deadly inhalants as are using marijuana, but the South Australian legislature is concerned about marijuana.)
See
Inhalant Abuse Called " The Silent Epidemic "
-- But Prohibitionist Propaganda Is Just Lying Too Loudly About Marijuana
For Anyone To Hear Anything Else – One More Way Marijuana Prohibition Kills
and
Fourth Graders Use Inhalants Much More Than Marijuana,
But Prohibitionist Propaganda Organization Press Release Shows
Both The Failure of Marijuana Prohibition and Their Failure To Understand Their Own Data
and
When A Drug Czar Lies About Marijuana, Kids Don’t Believe Him When He Tells The Truth About Inhalants.

The centre's Paul Dillon says the age of initiation into drug use is getting younger and younger.

" When you have got such high percentages of 12-year-olds having ever experimented with these drugs, it means we are seeing experimentation in primary schools, " he said.

" We have to change our view of where we do preventative drug education because if we are trying to do drug education at the age of 13, 14 and 15, we have missed the boat. "

Authorities find cannabis plants in prison
(MarijuanaNews note: Finally, this item was just too delicious. If they can’t stop marijuana growing in a prison, how can they think that they can stop it in homes?)
June 14, 2001

Prison authorities are investigating the discovery of cannabis plants growing on a prison farm in north Queensland.
